title: Questionnaire response templates and evidence matrix
content:
Purpose:
This working guide is intended for the security team and solutions engineers who prepare responses to customer security questionnaires and populate the trust center. It provides short, reusable answer templates, an evidence matrix linking questionnaire items to artifacts we can attach, and triage notes for RBAC v2, audit logs, SIEM export, and evidence automation.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Solutions engineering, customer success, security/compliance reviewers.
- Scope: SaaS hosted API and Dedicated capacity; notes for Private deployments when different. Not a legal position paper — for questionnaire responses only.

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Find the customer question and pick the template (A/B/C).
2) Attach evidence files listed in the matrix (artifact names below).
3) If an item is scope-limited or needs redaction, add the redaction note and escalate to security.
4) Track the response in JIRA (linked in linked_artifacts).

Section A — Short answer templates (pick and adapt)
- Template: Standard affirmative
  "We enforce role-based access controls across our control plane and customer resources. RBAC v2 provides least-privilege roles and audit logging for all control plane activity. We can provide architecture diagrams and policy snapshots on request."

- Template: Scoped / Sales-safe
  "Redwood supports role-based access controls for administrative and operational actions. For detailed role mappings and customer-specific roles in Dedicated and Private deployments, we will provide a redacted policy snapshot under NDA or via the trust center link provided."

- Template: Temporary exception
  "That capability is available for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted customers we offer compensating controls described in the attached hardening guide. Roadmap date available on request."

Section B — Common questionnaire questions and canonical responses
(Each entry: question summary -> canonical response -> required evidence artifacts)

1) Do you provide role-based access control? -> "Yes"
   Canonical response: "Yes. We have RBAC v2 for the control plane and per-customer role bindings for Dedicated/Private deployments. Roles are mapped to permission sets and enforced at the API layer. See 'RBAC policy snapshot' for mapping examples."
   Evidence: ["rbac-v2-policy-snapshot-2024-11.txt", "rbac-v2-design-diagram.png"]

2) How are administrative actions audited? -> "All admin actions are logged"
   Canonical response: "Administrative API calls, policy changes, and role assignments generate immutable audit entries stored in our audit log service and retained per customer SLO. See audit log schema and retention policy."
   Evidence: ["audit-log-schema-v2.json", "audit-retention-policy-ps-2024.pdf", "audit-sample-event-2024-10.json"]

3) Can logs be exported to customer SIEMs? -> "Yes, via SIEM export"
   Canonical response: "Customers can configure SIEM exports for audit logs and platform telemetry. Export supports streaming to secure S3 buckets, syslog endpoints, and partner-managed collectors. Exports include configurable filters and integrity metadata."
   Evidence: ["siem-export-implementation-notes.md", "siem-export-s3-manifest-example.csv"]

4) What is your incident detection and response process? -> "Formal IR process"
   Canonical response: "We maintain an incident response playbook, internal runbooks for triage and containment, and a public post-incident summary template for customers. For high-severity incidents affecting customer data we provide notifications per our contract."
   Evidence: ["incident-response-playbook-2024.docx", "post-incident-notification-template.txt"]

5) How do you protect customer data at rest and in transit? -> "Encryption in transit and at rest"
   Canonical response: "All customer data in transit is TLS 1.2+; stored data is encrypted with customer- or platform-managed keys depending on deployment. See KMS integrations and key rotation notes."
   Evidence: ["kms-integration-guide.pdf", "encryption-at-rest-tech-brief.md"]

Section C — Evidence matrix (mapping common questionnaire areas to artifacts and access instructions)
- RBAC / Permissions: rbac-v2-policy-snapshot-2024.txt; rbac-v2-design-diagram.png; github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-v2/pull/87 (design PR)
- Audit logs / Schema: audit-log-schema-v2.json; audit-sample-event-2024-10.json; audit-retention-policy-ps-2024.pdf
- SIEM export: siem-export-implementation-notes.md; siem-export-s3-manifest-example.csv; siem-export-security-assumptions.md
- Evidence automation: evidence-automation-runbook.md; evidence-export-playbook-2024.md; trust-package-assembly-script.sh
- Compliance artifacts: soc2-scoping-notes-2023.pdf; compliance-contacts.csv

Section D — RBAC v2 specifics to call out in answers
- Roles vs permission sets: RBAC v2 separates coarse-grained roles (operator, auditor, platform-admin) from fine-grained permission sets (model-deploy:create, model-deploy:promote, metrics:read).
- Customer scoping: For Hosted customers, role bindings are tenancy-aware and cannot reference other tenants' resources. For Dedicated/Private, customers may define custom role bindings controlled by their org admin.
- Admin approvals: Role changes are recorded and require a two-person approval flow for production-affecting roles (configurable by customer in Dedicated).
- Example artifact: rbac-change-log-2024-09.csv (contains redacted change records suitable for sharing under NDA).

Section E — Audit log schema summary (how to answer schema questions)
- Core fields: event_id, timestamp_utc, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_payload_hash, response_status, request_ip, user_agent, request_id, trace_id
- Integrity metadata: Each batch is signed with HMAC and includes a manifest with a sequence number and hash to support tamper-evidence.
- Retention: Default retention 90 days for Hosted, configurable up to customer SLA for Dedicated/Private.
- Typical customer Q template: "Provide the audit log schema and a sample event with redacted PII."
  Response: attach audit-log-schema-v2.json + audit-sample-event-2024-10.json (PII-redacted).

Section F — SIEM export practical notes (common pitfalls)
- Exports are eventually-consistent; customers needing strict ordering should use the sequence number in the manifest.
- Rate limits: Exports are subject to platform throughput limits; large customers should pre-provision dedicated export bandwidth via Dedicated contracts.
- Formats: JSON lines for S3, CEF for syslog; include example deliverables per evidence matrix.

Section G — Evidence automation and assembly
- We maintain scripts and runbooks to assemble a trust package: trust-package-assembly-script.sh and evidence-automation-runbook.md. These create a zip with artifacts and a manifest that can be delivered via secure link.
- Guidance when responding: prefer automated artifacts (schema, sample events, policy snapshots) over screenshots. Automated artifacts reduce manual redaction steps.

Section H — Example response snippets (copy-paste friendly)
- Encryption: "Data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256; keys are rotated annually and can be customer-managed for Private deployments. See attached kms-integration-guide.pdf."
- Log integrity: "Audit batches include a signed manifest and sequence numbers for tamper-evidence. We can provide a sample signed manifest under NDA."

Section I — Redaction & NDA guidance
- Default stance: share non-sensitive artifacts publicly via trust center. For any file that could contain customer identifiers, use a redacted copy and mark it with an escrow tag.
- If a customer asks for raw logs with identifiers, require an executed DPA + narrow-scope Addendum and route to Legal and Security.

Section J — Checklist before sending a response
- Pick canonical template and adapt (A/B/C).
- Attach artifacts from the evidence matrix.
- Verify no customer PII in shared artifacts (run evidence-automation redaction step).
- Add JIRA ticket and Confluence record for audit trail.
- Notify account owner and security reviewer.

Open questions / triage items:
- Retention SLA exceptions for shared Hosted customers beyond 90 days (Product to confirm pricing and process).
- Formalize a public subset of the audit-manifest format for the trust center (owner: Observability).

Next steps and owners:
- Leah Ortiz: produce a redacted example of 'rbac-change-log-2024-09.csv' suitable for trust center (due 2024-12-12).
- Marcus Chen: finalize the public audit-manifest spec and add it to trust center (due 2025-01-10).
- Aisha Patel: iterate on templates and distribute to SEs (ongoing).

Notes to self / working fragments:
- Keep two versions of each artifact: public (no identifiers) and NDA-ready (full, with request tracking).
- Consider adding a small interactive selector in the trust center to produce tailored packages (low effort, high impact).

Attachments (recommended artifact filenames to bundle):
- rbac-v2-policy-snapshot-2024.txt
- rbac-v2-design-diagram.png
- audit-log-schema-v2.json
- audit-sample-event-2024-10.json
- audit-retention-policy-ps-2024.pdf
- siem-export-implementation-notes.md
- siem-export-s3-manifest-example.csv
- evidence-automation-runbook.md
- trust-package-assembly-script.sh

End of doc.

(Working doc — expect incremental edits and more sample answers for vertical-specific questionnaires.)
